title: The Tuxedo Band at private parties
summary: She adds that the Tuxedo Band was the first Negro jazz band at white social events, playing her birthday party and fraternity parties.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I remember now that, um, the first Negro jazz band that played at, uh, any social white artists in New Orleans was called a Tuxedo Band. And South Stan was not the leader, but he was a member of the band. And that, they played for private parties. And they might have played at the country club, but that was before my time. So I wouldn't know it was, I would say, in, around 19, 18, or 19.
Well, what about this party? How, how old you were? You were born in 1905, right? Mm-hmm. So, how old you were at this party? And, uh, tradition?

Oh, well, he played at the birthday party. I, let's see, it might, I was either 14 or 16, I can't remember. And, uh, it was just a dance at home. And this same Tuxedo Band played at several of the parties, and they also used to play at the, little, um, the fraternity, the high school fraternity party. What was it? About seventh stuff.
